s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: pertaining to not being able to come to some agreement
s.g: to be in disagreement; to not agree with; to be unable to agree

s.dp: Understand › Lack of Capacity for Understanding
s.d: pertaining to a lack of capacity for insight and understanding
s.c: Care must be exercised in the rendering of ἀσύνετος in ⟦Matthew 15:16|Matthew 15:16⟧ and ⟦Romans 1:21|Romans 1:21⟧, since a lack of capacity for understanding may result from mental deficiencies or from a lack of the proper use of mental capacity. It is, of course, this latter meaning which is involved in the use of ἀσύνετος in these contexts.

s.dp: Association › Establish or Confirm a Relation
s.d: pertaining to not being bound or not regarding oneself as bound by any covenant or agreement
s.g: not keeping a promise; not abiding by an agreement
s.c: It is also possible to translate ἀσύνθετος in ⟦Romans 1:31|Romans 1:31⟧ as ‘they feel no obligation to keep their agreements’ or ‘they do not feel bound to do what they have promised to do.’

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: a state of safety and security, implying a complete lack of danger
s.c: In some languages safety or security is expressed in a negative way, for example, ‘without any danger’ or ‘without anything that might possibly harm.’

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Believe To Be True
s.d: a state of certainty with regard to a belief
s.c: It is also possible to render ⟦Luke 1:4|Luke 1:4⟧ as ‘so that you may know that those things that you have been taught are certainly true.’

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: pertaining to a state of safety and security, and hence free from danger

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Believe To Be True
s.d: pertaining to being certain and thus completely believable
s.g: worthy of being believed; certainly true; completely believable

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: to cause something to be secure in the sense of something which could not be tampered with or opened
s.g: to make secure; to be guarded

s.dp: Attachment › Fasten, Stick To
s.d: to fasten something securely
s.c: It is possible that in ⟦Acts 16:24|Acts 16:24⟧ τὸ ξύλον designates ‘stocks,’ namely, two pieces of wood through which the feet could be placed so as to make a prisoner immobile (see LN 6.21).

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: pertaining to a state of safety and security, and hence free from danger
s.c: In ⟦Acts 16:23|Acts 16:23⟧ ἀσφαλῶς does not refer to the safety of the prisoners but to the security with which they were guarded, hence eliminating any danger of their escaping.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Believe To Be True
s.d: pertaining to being certain and thus completely believable
s.g: worthy of being believed; certainly true; completely believable

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Act Shamefully
s.d: to act in defiance of social and moral standards, with resulting disgrace, embarrassment, and shame
s.g: to act shamefully; indecent behavior; shameful deed
s.c: Behavior involving disgrace, embarrassment, and shame is often expressed in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘to bury one’s face,’ ‘to hide one’s eyes,’ or ‘to feel stabbed by people’s eyes.’ Since shame is seemingly a universal type of feeling, there is usually no difficulty involved in obtaining a satisfactory equivalent.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Act Shamefully
s.d: to act in defiance of social and moral standards, with resulting disgrace, embarrassment, and shame
s.g: to act shamefully; indecent behavior; shameful deed
s.c: Behavior involving disgrace, embarrassment, and shame is often expressed in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘to bury one’s face,’ ‘to hide one’s eyes,’ or ‘to feel stabbed by people’s eyes.’ Since shame is seemingly a universal type of feeling, there is usually no difficulty involved in obtaining a satisfactory equivalent.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Shame, Disgrace, Humiliation
s.d: a state which is or should be regarded as causing shame

s.dp: Features of Objects › Beautiful, Ugly
s.d: pertaining to being unattractive or unseemly

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sensible Behavior, Senseless Behavior
s.d: behavior which shows lack of concern or thought for the consequences of an action
s.c: In some languages ἀσωτία in ⟦Ephesians 5:18|Ephesians 5:18⟧ may be rendered as ‘what one does without being able to think about it’ or ‘what one does when the mind is absent.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sensible Behavior, Senseless Behavior
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀσωτία<SDBG:ἀσωτία:000000>} ‘senseless deeds,’ {D:88.96}) pertaining to senseless, reckless behavior
s.c: In a number of languages ‘to live recklessly’ is ‘to live without thinking’ or ‘to live without being concerned.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Laziness, Idleness
s.d: to refuse to be engaged in the efforts of work
s.g: to do nothing; to be idle; to be lazy
s.c: Traditional translations have often interpreted ἀτακτέω in an etymological sense of ‘not being ordered’ and hence with a meaning of ‘to behave in a disorderly manner,’ but this is quite contrary to the context.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Laziness, Idleness
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀτακτέω<SDBG:ἀτακτέω:000000>} ‘to do nothing,’ {D:88.246}) pertaining to refusing to work

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Laziness, Idleness
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀτακτέω<SDBG:ἀτακτέω:000000>} ‘to do nothing,’ {D:88.246}) pertaining to refusing to work
s.c: For a discussion of ἀτακτέω in the related context of ⟦2 Thessalonians 3:7|2 Thessalonians 3:7⟧, see LN 88.246.

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: pertaining to being without offspring

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to fix one’s eyes on some object continually and intensely
s.g: to look straight at; to stare at; to keep one’s eyes fixed on
s.c: The expression ‘could not keep their eyes fixed on’ may be rendered as ‘could not keep looking at’ or ‘could not continue to look at.’

s.dp: Relations › Dissociation
s.d: a marker of negatively linked elements{N:001}
s.g: without; not with; no relationship to; apart from; independent of
s.c: The phrase ἄτερ ὄχλου may be interpreted to mean ‘without the people knowing about it’ or ‘in the absence of the multitude.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Treat Badly
s.d: to treat someone in a shameful and dishonorable manner
s.c: It is often possible to translate ἀτιμάζω in ⟦Mark 12:4|Mark 12:4⟧ as ‘to make him suffer the way he should not.’

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: to cause someone to have low status involving dishonor and disrespect
s.g: to cause to be dishonored; to cause to suffer dishonor
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘causing someone to be dishonored’ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to cause someone to be laughed at’ or ‘to cause people to wag their heads at someone’ or ‘to cause people to turn away from someone.’

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: a state of dishonor or disrespect as a negative of {L:τιμή<SDBG:τιμή:000000>}[a] ‘honor, respect’ ({D:87.4})

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: pertaining to being of low status on the basis of not having honor or respect

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Atmospheric Objects
s.d: a hot steamy vapor
s.c: An important connotation in the use of the term ἀτμίς is the fact that it disappears so readily. This is a particularly significant element in ⟦James 4:14|James 4:14⟧. The closest equivalent of ἀτμίς is normally a term which refers to the steam rising from a boiling pot or cauldron.

s.dp: Time › Indefinite Units of Time: Age, Lifetime, Interval, Period
s.d: an extremely short unit of time

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Bad, Evil, Harmful, Damaging
s.d: pertaining to not being in accordance with what is right, appropriate, or fitting
s.g: not fitting; what should not be done; bad

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Unusual, Different From the Ordinary
s.d: pertaining to that which is unusual, and generally with the implication of harmful or dangerous

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a seaport in Pamphylia

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to cause something to be clearly evident
s.g: to cause to be seen; to cause to be clear to

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
s.d: the point of time when the day begins{N:001}

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Latin title given to Emperor Octavian and equivalent to a proper name; ruled from 27 B.C. to 14 A.D.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Arrogance, Haughtiness, Pride
s.d: pertaining to being arrogant as the result of self-will and stubbornness
s.c: In a number of languages ‘arrogant’ may be expressed as ‘thinking one is so much better than everyone else’ or ‘always looking down on other people’ or ‘always saying, I am better.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Be Willing
s.d: pertaining to being willing, with the implication of choice
s.g: willing; of one’s own free will

s.dp: Control, Rule › Control, Restrain
s.d: to control in a domineering manner
s.c: ‘To control in a domineering manner’ is often expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to shout orders at,’ ‘to act like a chief toward,’ or ‘to bark at.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: derivative of αὐλός flute

s.dp: Constructions › Open Constructions
s.d: a walled enclosure either to enclose human activity or to protect livestock
s.c: A sheepfold may be described in some languages as ‘a place for sheep with a wall built around it’ or ‘a corral for sheep’ or ‘a place for protecting sheep.’

s.dp: Constructions › Buildings
s.d: an open area enclosed by structures within a building complex, such as the temple, a palace, or a house; or any dwelling having such an enclosed open area (often a relatively elaborate structure)

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: (derivative of {L:αὐλός<SDBG:αὐλός:000000>} ‘flute,’ {D:6.87}) one who plays the flute

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: to lodge in a place during the night

s.dp: Artifacts › Musical Instruments
s.d: a musical wind instrument consisting of a tube with a series of finger holes used to alter the tone

s.dp: Quantity › Increase, Decrease
s.d: to increase in the extent of or in the instances of an activity or state
s.g: to increase; to grow; to spread; to extend
s.c: If one assumes that ἐπίγνωσις in ⟦Colossians 1:10|Colossians 1:10⟧ is to be understood in the sense of ‘knowledge about’ (see LN 28.18), then one may translate this expression as ‘you will know more and more about God,’ but if ἐπίγνωσις is to be understood in the sense of ‘to experience knowledge’ (see LN 28.2), one may ‘you will know God more and more’ or ‘you will come to know more and more what God does.’

s.dp: Quantity › Increase, Decrease
s.d: to cause something to increase
s.g: to cause to increase; to increase

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Grow, Growth
s.d: to grow, to increase in size, whether of animate beings or of plants
s.c: In a number of languages one must make a clear distinction in the choice of terms referring to the growth of an animate being (animal or human) and the growth of plants.

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: to increase in status
s.g: to become more important; to enjoy greater respect or honor
s.c: In some languages the increase or decrease of respect or honor must be expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘he must become more of a chief while I become more of a follower’ or ‘he must become a big man while I become a small man.’

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: to increase in the degree of a state
s.c: It would be possible to interpret αὐξάνομαι in ⟦2 Corinthians 10:15|2 Corinthians 10:15⟧ as being quantitative, but with an expression of state such as πίστις, intensity of degree seems to be more appropriate. In a number of languages, however, it may be necessary to render this expression in ⟦2 Corinthians 10:15|2 Corinthians 10:15⟧ as ‘hoping that you may trust more and more.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Grow, Growth
s.d: to grow, to increase in size, whether of animate beings or of plants
s.c: In a number of languages one must make a clear distinction in the choice of terms referring to the growth of an animate being (animal or human) and the growth of plants|In ⟦Colossians 2:19|Colossians 2:19⟧ αὔξησις is used figuratively in the sense that the reference of ‘body’ is the church rather than a physical body. Normally a term for ‘growth’ would imply not only size but also number, that is to say, the growth of the church would be in terms of the increase of members of the church, though it might refer to spiritual maturity. In some instances, however, it may be necessary to specify ‘growth in numbers’ so as to avoid the implication which might be derived from the context, namely, that the church is simply a building which gets bigger and bigger.

s.dp: Time › Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
s.d: a day following the day of a discourse

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time subsequent to another point of time and indicating imminence, that is to say, the subsequent event is regarded as almost begun

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Act Harshly
s.d: pertaining to being exacting, with a possible implication of being severe in either a favorable or unfavorable sense

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Content, Satisfied
s.d: the state of being content with one’s circumstances or lot in life
s.g: self-content; contentment; contentment with what one has

s.dp: Adequate, Qualified
s.d: a state of adequacy or sufficiency
s.g: what is adequate; what is sufficient; what is needed; adequacy
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of this expression in ⟦2 Corinthians 9:8|2 Corinthians 9:8⟧ may be ‘always having all that you need’ or, stated negatively, ‘not lacking in anything.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Content, Satisfied
s.d: pertaining to being happy or content with what one has
s.g: content with what one has; content with the circumstances in which one exists

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: pertaining to one who is condemned as the result of his own actions

s.dp: Relations › Cause and/or Reason
s.d: pertaining to being self-caused (or possibly, without evident cause){N:001}
s.g: without any cause; without something to cause it; by itself
s.c: In some languages one can only express ‘opened … by itself’ in ⟦Acts 12:10|Acts 12:10⟧ by ‘opened … nobody made it open.’

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: one who has personally seen an event and thus has personal knowledge and can be expected to attest to the occurrence of such an event

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Same or Equivalent Kind or Class
s.d: pertaining to that which is identical to something
a set phrase, similar to (1) in meaning, with the force of association

s.dp: Discourse Referentials › Whom or What Spoken or Written About
s.d: a reference to a definite person or persons spoken or written about (with an added feature of emphasis in the nominative forms)
s.g: he; him; she; her; it; they; them

s.dp: Discourse Referentials › Emphatic Adjunct
s.d: a marker of emphasis by calling attention to the distinctiveness of the lexical item with which it occurs (used for all persons, genders, and numbers){N:001}
s.g: -self; -selves (for example, myself, yourself, yourselves, ourselves, himself, herself, itself, themselves)

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Here, There
s.d: a position either near or far from the speaker, writer, or viewpoint character

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: of a person’s own hands
s.c: But in rendering ⟦Acts 27:19|Acts 27:19⟧, it may be somewhat superfluous or even misleading to speak about throwing over the ships tackle ‘with their own hands.’ The emphasis is not upon the hands so much as the activity of the people aboard the ship. Therefore, one may better translate ⟦Acts 27:19|Acts 27:19⟧ as ‘they themselves threw the ships tackle overboard.’ Obviously, more than the hands were employed in this activity.

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Darkness
s.d: pertaining to being not only dark, but also dirty and miserable
s.c: In ⟦2 Peter 1:19|2 Peter 1:19⟧ αὐχμηρός may also suggest moral degradation, and in English the phrase ‘filthy darkness’ could suggest this type of meaning.

s.dp: Existence in Space › Put, Place
s.d: to put or take something away from its normal location{N:001}
s.g: to put away; to put out of the way; to remove
s.c: In the context of ⟦Luke 22:50|Luke 22:50⟧ it may be far more appropriate to translate ‘and he cut off his right ear.’

s.dp: Aspect › Cease, Stop
s.d: to cause to cease, implying that someone is no longer permitted to enjoy or participate in some state or activity
s.g: to take away (from); to cause to no longer do

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to cause a state to cease{N:002}
s.g: to do away with; to remove; to eliminate

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: pertaining to not being able to be seen or known, and thus to be hidden
s.c: It is possible to render ‘that can be hidden from him’ as ‘that people can keep God from seeing’ or ‘that people can prevent God from knowing about.’

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Destroy
s.d: to destroy the value or use of something
s.c: See LN 4.49.

s.dp: Features of Objects › Beautiful, Ugly
s.d: to cause something to be unattractive or unsightly
s.g: to make unsightly; to disfigure; to make ugly

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to become such as not to be seen
s.g: to become invisible (in the passive, to disappear, to vanish)
s.c: In a number of instances one can best render ‘vanishes’ as ‘cannot be seen’ or ‘suddenly people cannot see it.’

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Exist
s.d: to cease to exist, with the implication of no longer being evident or visible
s.g: to cease to exist; to disappear; to die; disappearance

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Exist
s.d: to cease to exist, with the implication of no longer being evident or visible
s.g: to cease to exist; to disappear; to die; disappearance

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀφανίζομαι<SDBG:ἀφανίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to become invisible,’ {D:24.27}) pertaining to that which becomes invisible

s.dp: Constructions › Miscellaneous Constructions
s.c: The term ἀφεδρών occurs only in ⟦Matthew 15:17|Matthew 15:17⟧ and ⟦Mark 7:19|Mark 7:19⟧ and may be rendered in a number of languages as ‘place of defecation.’ In some languages, however, a reference to a toilet may seem inappropriate for the Scriptures, and it is possible to translate a passage such as ⟦Matthew 15:17|Matthew 15:17⟧ as ‘goes into the stomach and then passes on out.’ The meaning is thus clear without a specific reference to a latrine or toilet.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Self-Control, Lack of Self-Control
s.d: severe self-control, suggesting an ascetic and unsparing attitude

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Humility
s.d: humility associated with simplicity of life

s.dp: Reconciliation, Forgiveness › Forgiveness
s.d: to remove the guilt resulting from wrongdoing
s.c: It is extremely important to note that the focus in the meanings of ἀφίημι, ἄφεσις, and ἀπολύω is upon the guilt of the wrongdoer and not upon the wrongdoing itself. The event of wrongdoing is not undone, but the guilt resulting from such an event is pardoned. To forgive, therefore, means essentially to remove the guilt resulting from wrongdoing.|Some languages make a clear distinction between guilt and sin, and terms for forgiveness are therefore related to guilt and not to the wrongdoing. Therefore, ‘to forgive sins’ is literally ‘to forgive guilt.’ Though terms for ‘forgiveness’ are often literally ‘to wipe out,’ ‘to blot out,’ or ‘to do away with,’ it is obviously not possible to blot out or to wipe out an event, but it is possible to remove or obliterate the guilt.

s.dp: Control, Rule › Release, Set Free
s.d: the process of setting free or liberating

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: part of the joints of the body which binds the different parts together
s.c: In some languages the ligaments may be spoken of as ‘the ropes of the body’ or ‘the strings of the body.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: the state of not being subject to decay, leading to death
s.c: It is possible to translate this clause as ‘it will be raised and will never again die.’|In rendering ‘immortality’ it may be necessary to employ an entire clause, for example, ‘that people will not die.’ However, in ⟦2 Timothy 1:10|2 Timothy 1:10⟧ ‘life and immortality’ may be best understood as a phrase in which ‘immortality’ is a qualification of ‘life,’ and therefore one may translate ‘revealing immortal life through the gospel’ or ‘revealing by means of the good news the life that does not end.’

s.dp: Aspect › Cease, Stop
s.d: a continuous state or process, with the implication that the state or process in question is not interrupted by death
s.c: A number of scholars, however, insist that ἀφθαρσία in ⟦Ephesians 6:24|Ephesians 6:24⟧ must be understood in the sense of ‘immortality’ or ‘eternity’ as a temporal expression, but one which can be rendered as ‘with undying love.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: pertaining to being not subject to decay and death

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to cause (or permit) a person or persons to leave a particular location{N:001}
s.g: to let go away; to dismiss

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move away from, with the implication of resulting separation{N:002}

s.dp: Existence in Space › Put, Place
s.d: to let something be put behind in a place

s.dp: Existence in Space › Remain, Stay
s.d: to permit something to continue in a place

s.dp: Association › Marriage, Divorce
s.d: to dissolve the marriage bond
s.c: Expressions for divorce are often based on terms meaning literally ‘to send away,’ ‘to separate from,’ or ‘to leave one another.’ However, in a number of languages idiomatic expressions are employed, for example ‘to send him off with his clothes,’ ‘to untie the knot between them,’ or ‘to throw away her hearthstones.’|Some persons have attempted to make an important distinction between ἀφίημι in ⟦1 Corinthians 7:11|1 Corinthians 7:11⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 7:13|1 Corinthians 7:13⟧ and χωρίζω in ⟦1 Corinthians 7:15|1 Corinthians 7:15⟧ on the assumption that ἀφίημι implies legal divorce, while χωρίζω only relates to separation. Such a distinction, however, seems to be quite artificial.

s.dp: Reconciliation, Forgiveness › Forgiveness
s.d: to remove the guilt resulting from wrongdoing
s.c: It is extremely important to note that the focus in the meanings of ἀφίημι, ἄφεσις, and ἀπολύω is upon the guilt of the wrongdoer and not upon the wrongdoing itself. The event of wrongdoing is not undone, but the guilt resulting from such an event is pardoned. To forgive, therefore, means essentially to remove the guilt resulting from wrongdoing.|Some languages make a clear distinction between guilt and sin, and terms for forgiveness are therefore related to guilt and not to the wrongdoing. Therefore, ‘to forgive sins’ is literally ‘to forgive guilt.’ Though terms for ‘forgiveness’ are often literally ‘to wipe out,’ ‘to blot out,’ or ‘to do away with,’ it is obviously not possible to blot out or to wipe out an event, but it is possible to remove or obliterate the guilt.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Owe, Debt, Cancel
s.d: to release a person from the obligation of repaying what is owed
s.g: to cancel a debt; to forgive a debt

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: to no longer pay attention to previous beliefs
s.g: to refuse to listen to; to reject

s.dp: Aspect › Cease, Stop
s.d: to stop doing something, with the implication of complete cessation
s.g: to give up; to stop; to quit

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to cease, of a state
s.g: to cease; to stop; to leave

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to leave it to someone to do something, with the implication of distancing oneself from the event
s.g: to let; to allow; to leave it to

s.dp: Case › Agent of a Numerable Event
s.d: a marker of an agent relation with numerable events, with the implication of something which proceeds from an agent
s.g: to produce; to make; to give

s.dp: Communication › Interpret, Mean, Explain
s.d: (an idiom, possibly an adage, literally: let the dead bury their dead) the matter in question is not the real issue
s.g: that is not what I mean; that is not the issue; that is not the point
s.c: Some scholars, however, understand this expression as merely a figurative reference to various types of people and thus translate ‘let those who are spiritually dead take care of their own dead.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to send away the spirit) interpreted by some as implying voluntarily laying down one’s life, but such an inference is not justified by normal Greek usage)

s.dp: Know › Known [the content of knowledge]
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀφικνέομαι ‘to move up to a point,’ not occurring in the NT) to become known as the result of information reaching its destination

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: pertaining to not loving what is good
s.g: not loving what is good; being an enemy to what is good; being against what is good

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: pertaining to not being desirous or greedy for money
s.g: not loving wealth; one who does not love money

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: motion away from a reference point with emphasis upon the departure, but without implications as to any resulting state of separation or rupture{N:001}
s.g: to go away; to depart; to leave

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Rebellion
s.d: to cause people to rebel against or to reject authority
s.g: to incite to revolt; to cause to rebel

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move away from, with emphasis upon separation and possible lack of concern for what has been left
s.g: to go away; to depart; to leave

s.dp: Association › Join, Begin To Associate
s.d: to abandon a former relationship or association, or to dissociate (a type of reversal of beginning to associate){N:001}
s.g: to fall away; to forsake; to turn away

s.dp: Association › Limit or Avoid Association
s.d: purposely to avoid association with someone{N:002}
s.g: to shun; to avoid; to keep away from; to have nothing to do with

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to an extremely short period of time between a previous state or event and a subsequent state or event (in a number of contexts there is the implication of unexpectedness; but this seems to be a derivative of the context as a whole and not a part of the meaning of the lexical items)

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Fear, Terror, Alarm
s.d: pertaining to being without fear
s.c: An adverb such as ἀφόβως often corresponds to a clause in other languages. Accordingly, ‘dare to preach the message fearlessly’ must be rendered in some languages as ‘dare to preach the message without being afraid of anyone.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Act Shamefully
s.d: pertaining to disgraceful behavior which shows no regard or fear for social sanctions
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀφόβως in ⟦Jude 1:12|Jude 1:12⟧, see ἀφόβως LN 53.60.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Worship, Reverence
s.d: pertaining to being without reverence or awe for God
s.c: It is also possible that ἀφόβως in ⟦Jude 1:12|Jude 1:12⟧ should be understood as simply ‘being without fear’ or ‘boldly’ (LN 25.253). For another interpretation of ἀφόβως in ⟦Jude 1:12|Jude 1:12⟧, see ἀφόβως LN 88.151.

s.dp: Comparison
s.d: to be like or similar to something else
s.g: to be like; to resemble; to be similar to

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: to keep thinking about, without having one’s attention distracted
s.g: to think about; to fix one’s attention on

s.dp: Learn
s.d: to acquire information, with focus presumably upon the source of such information
s.g: to learn about; to find out about

s.dp: Association › Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
s.d: to exclude or remove someone from an association
s.g: to exclude; to separate; to get rid of
s.c: It is, of course, possible to translate ἀφορίζω in ⟦Luke 6:22|Luke 6:22⟧ as ‘not to welcome,’ but the emphasis of ἀφορίζω is to exclude from a relationship which has previously existed. One may therefore translate ⟦Luke 6:22|Luke 6:22⟧ as ‘happy are you … when people no longer welcome you in their company … because of the Son of Man.’ By introducing the temporal element ‘no longer,’ the fact of exclusion is made clear.

s.dp: Control, Rule › Assign to a Role or Function
s.d: to set aside a person for a particular task or function{N:001}
s.g: to appoint; to set apart for

s.dp: Whole, Unite, Part, Divide › Separate
s.d: to separate into two or more parts or groups, often by some intervening space
s.g: to separate; to set one apart from another

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Favorable Circumstances or State
s.d: a set of circumstances favorable for a particular activity or endeavor
s.c: In a number of languages it may be necessary to translate ἀφορμή opportunity in different ways depending upon the context. For example, in ⟦Romans 7:8|Romans 7:8⟧ ἀφορμή may be rendered as ‘a good chance to …’ In ⟦Galatians 5:13|Galatians 5:13⟧ ἀφορμή may be rendered as ‘a good way for …,’ and in ⟦1 Timothy 5:14|1 Timothy 5:14⟧ ἀφορμή may be rendered ‘as a good reason for …’

s.dp: Relations › Cause and/or Reason
s.d: an unwarranted reason for some event

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: to cause or to produce the foaming up of a liquid (restricted in the NT to the foaming at the mouth of a person experiencing an epileptic seizure)
s.g: to foam up; to foam at the mouth
s.c: Since foaming at the mouth is so characteristic of epileptic seizures, there should be no difficulty in finding a rather specific term to identify this type of event.

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀφρίζω<SDBG:ἀφρίζω:000000>} ‘to cause foaming of a liquid,’ {D:14.28}) a frothy, foaming mass or substance
s.c: Though ἀφρός may refer to any type of foam or frothy substance, in ⟦Luke 9:39|Luke 9:39⟧ the reference is clearly to frothy saliva coming out of the mouth, something which is typical of persons experiencing an epileptic seizure. A number of languages have quite specific terms for this type of foaming or frothing at the mouth, expressed literally in some instances as ‘his saliva was bubbling out of his mouth’ or ‘the water of his mouth came out in bubbles.’

s.dp: Understand › Lack of Capacity for Understanding
s.d: the state of not using one’s capacity for understanding

s.dp: Understand › Lack of Capacity for Understanding
s.d: pertaining to not employing one’s understanding, particularly in practical matters
s.c: It is possible that ἄφρων in ⟦Romans 2:20|Romans 2:20⟧ (παιδευτὴν ἀφρόνων ‘instructor of the foolish’) refers to people who are simply uninstructed or ignorant, since ἀφρόνων could be parallel with νηπίων, occurring in the same verse. On the other hand, there appears to be a contrast in the meanings of ἀφρόνων and νηπίων because of the distinctiveness in meanings of παιδευτήν and διδάσκαλον. Therefore, ἄφρων in ⟦Romans 2:20|Romans 2:20⟧ is better understood as referring to those who act foolishly because they do not use their potential for understanding.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sleep, Waking
s.d: to begin to sleep
s.c: It would obviously be a mistake to try to imitate the English idiom ‘to fall asleep,’ for this might be understood as ‘to go to sleep and as a result fall down’ or even ‘to fall down and then remain unconscious.’

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: pertaining to not being able to speak or talk
s.g: dumb; mute; unable to speak; incapable of talking

s.dp: Communication › Interpret, Mean, Explain
s.d: pertaining to being without meaning
s.c: Rather than use a double negative expression in rendering this phrase in ⟦1 Corinthians 14:10|1 Corinthians 14:10⟧, it may be better in many languages to use a positive expression, for example, ‘yet all can be understood’ or ‘yet all have meaning.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a Roman province including the most important parts of Greece

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian at Corinth

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Thankful, Grateful
s.d: pertaining to a complete lack of thankfulness
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀχάριστος in ⟦Luke 6:35|Luke 6:35⟧, see ἀχάριστος LN 33.353.

s.dp: Communication › Thanks
s.d: pertaining to not being thankful
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀχάριστος in ⟦Luke 6:35|Luke 6:35⟧, see ἀχάριστος LN 25.101.

s.dp: Perform, Do › Make, Create
s.d: pertaining to what has not been made by someone
s.g: not made by human hands; not man-made

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: (a possible idiom, literally: mistiness and darkness fall) a serious impairment of sight, possibly involving total blindness
s.g: dark mistiness occurs (to someone); to become blind

s.dp: Value › Useful, Useless
s.d: pertaining to not being useful
s.c: In a number of languages usefulness or lack of usefulness can only be expressed in terms of a verb meaning ‘to help,’ so that in ⟦Philemon 1:11|Philemon 1:11⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘at one time he did not help you at all and now he can help both you and me.’

s.dp: Communication › Praise
s.d: pertaining to being without such qualities as deserve praise or commendation
s.g: not deserving special praise; not worthy of particular commendation

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Licentiousness, Perversion
s.d: to engage in behavior which is totally wrong and harmful
s.g: to go wrong; to become perverse

s.dp: Value › Useful, Useless
s.d: pertaining to not being useful
s.c: In a number of languages usefulness or lack of usefulness can only be expressed in terms of a verb meaning ‘to help,’ so that in ⟦Philemon 1:11|Philemon 1:11⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘at one time he did not help you at all and now he can help both you and me.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: the continuous extent of time up to a point{N:001}
s.g: until; to; at last; at length
s.c: The phrase εἰ μὴ ὅταν is often translated as ‘until’ (for example, μηδενὶ ἅ εἶδον διηγήσωνταιεἰ μὴ ὅταν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ ‘not to tell anybody what they have seen until the Son of Man has risen from death’ ⟦Mark 9:9|Mark 9:9⟧), but this phrase may be analyzed as meaning ‘if it is not when,’ an expression which is semantically equivalent to ‘until.’

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time which is subsequent to a duration and simultaneous with another point of time

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension To a Goal
s.d: extension up to or as far as a goal{N:002}
s.g: to; up to; as far as

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time prior to another point of time

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
s.d: an extent of time of the same length as another extent or unit of time

s.dp: Plants › Non-Fruit Parts of Plants
s.d: the husks of grain
s.c: Chaff may be referred to in some languages as ‘the empty part of the grain’ or ‘the leaves of the grain’ or ‘the refuse of the grain.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Honesty, Sincerity
s.d: pertaining to not speaking falsehood

s.dp: Features of Objects › Sweet, Bitter, Tasteless
s.d: the taste of wormwood, a bitter-tasting herb used as a cure for intestinal worms; compare {D:3.21}
s.c: As already noted in LN 3.21, the meaning of ἄψινθος in ⟦Revelation 8:11|Revelation 8:11⟧ is not that the waters turned into a particular plant but that the waters came to be as bitter as the plant in question.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: pertaining to a state of not having life
s.c: In some translations it may seem strange or even meaningless to speak of ‘musical instruments’ as being ‘lifeless’ or ‘not alive,’ since everyone would obviously know such a fact. It may therefore be necessary to translate as ‘even musical instruments like the flute and the harp, which are obviously not alive, nevertheless produce a sound.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Semitic deity

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: the capital of Babylonia
s.c: Βαβυλών also occurs as a symbol of demonic world power (⟦Revelation 14:8|Revelation 14:8⟧; ⟦Revelation 16:19|Revelation 16:19⟧).

s.dp: Status › Position, Rank
s.d: a standing in society implying rank or status

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › High, Low, Deep
s.d: the distance beneath a surface
s.c: In some languages it may be best to say ‘because there was not much soil’ ⟦Matthew 13:5|Matthew 13:5⟧.

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › High, Low, Deep
s.d: a place that is deep

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: an extreme point on a scale of extent

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Regions Below the Surface of the Earth
s.d: a place or region which is low
s.c: As in the case of ὕψωμα (LN 1.13), βάθος may be interpreted as a supernatural force ().|The phrase κατώτερα μέρη τῆς γῆς ‘the lower parts of the earth’ may likewise refer to ‘the world below’ as in εἰς τὰ κατώτερα μέρη τῆς γῆς ‘down into the lower parts of the earth’ ⟦Romans 8:39|Romans 8:39⟧ (see LN 83.54). Some scholars, however, understand this expression as being a reference to the earth which is low in contrast with heaven. On the basis of such an interpretation one may render ⟦Romans 8:39|Romans 8:39⟧ as ‘he came down to the earth itself.’

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Powers
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:βάθος<SDBG:βάθος:000000>}[a] ‘depth,’ {D:81.8}) supernatural powers in the region below the earth
s.c: See LN 12.46 for an illustrative passage in ⟦Romans 8:38|Romans 8:38⟧, ⟦Romans 8:39|Romans 8:39⟧. For another interpretation of βάθος in ⟦Romans 8:39|Romans 8:39⟧, see βάθος LN 1.18.|As in the case of ὕψωμα (LN 12.46), βάθος has been interpreted by some as indicating merely the distance which a person might be separated from God, but most scholars assume that the reference here is to ‘the powers of the world below.’

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:βάθος<SDBG:βάθος:000000>}[a] ‘depth,’ {D:81.8}) the content of knowledge which is very difficult to know
s.g: deep secrets; secrets difficult to find out about
s.c: Only rarely can one use a literal rendering of τὰ βαθέα or τὰ βάθη in referring to secrets. In some instances it may be possible to use an expression such as ‘far away’ or ‘distant,’ and in other cases one can use expressions meaning ‘hard’ or ‘difficult.’ More often than not, however, the closest equivalent of τὰ βαθέα and τὰ βάθη in this type of context is either an expression of degree using a term such as ‘very’ (for example, ‘that which is very secret’) or an expression implying ‘that which is hidden’ or ‘that which is difficult to discover.’
